text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns more total value to the group than keeping it, but self-interest favors free-riding since contributing only returns a fraction back to the contributor. The dominant strategy is zero contribution, yet mutual cooperation benefits everyone more—since this is finite and repeated over 10 rounds, I'm weighing whether to start cooperatively.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns 0.3 to every member, so contributing is individually costly (0.3 return vs 1 kept) even though full cooperation maximizes group payoff at 24 per round. The dominant strategy is to free-ride, but I'm weighing whether cooperating anyway makes sense given the group dynamic.

With 10 repeated rounds, I'm thinking through how reputation and reciprocity might sustain some cooperation despite the free-rider incentive.

I'll open with a moderate contribution, say around 10 tokens, to signal willingness to cooperate and see how the group responds before adjusting my strategy.

Round 1 worked out to 16 points for me since others only contributed 10 total. Now for round 2, cooperation seems weak so I'm weighing whether to keep contributing 10, working through how my payoff depends on how much others put in.

My marginal return per token I give up is still negative for me individually, so defection is technically dominant. But since others gave low, I could try scaling back to something like 5 as a middle ground to test reciprocity rather than fully defecting.
